parsed.title: Prellberg–Stanton overpartition coefficient nonnegativity conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and write the resulting formal power series in $q$ as a polynomial or power series with coefficients in the relevant coefficient ring. **Prellberg–Stanton overpartition conjecture.** For all positive integers $n$, the coefficients of

$$
(1-q)\frac{(-q^n)_n}{(q^n)_n}+q
$$

are non-negative. This conjecture proposes an overpartition analogue of the nonnegativity result of Prellberg and Stanton; the source reports numerical evidence but gives no proof or resolution.
parsed.source_name: Jehanne Dousse and Byungchan Kim, “An overpartition analogue of q-binomial coefficients, II: combinatorial proofs and (q,t)-log concavity”, arXiv:1701.07915 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.07915

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

parsed.title: Finite-commutative-ring product-of-difference-sets conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $\alpha>0$. A finite commutative ring is a ring $R$ with finitely many elements, and for a set $E\subset R$ write

$$
(E-E)\cdot(E-E)=\{(e_1-e_2)(e_3-e_4)\mid e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4\in E\}.
$$

**Finite-ring product-of-difference-sets conjecture.** There exist $N$ and $k$, depending only on $\alpha$, such that for every finite commutative ring $R$ with $|R|\ge N$ and every set $E\subset R$ satisfying $|E|\ge\alpha|R|$, the set $(E-E)\cdot(E-E)$ contains a subring $R_0$ such that

$$
|R|/|R_0|\le k.
$$

This is proposed as a quantitative analogue of the paper's results for integer and finite cyclic settings. The source presents it as a belief for finite commutative rings and gives no resolution.
parsed.source_name: Alexander Fish, “On product of difference sets for sets of positive density”, arXiv:1702.02544 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.02544

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

parsed.title: Generalized-Fibonacci form of pre-moments for fixed $d$
parsed.statement:
Let $X_{d,n}$ be the size of a uniformly random $(n,dn-1)$-core partition with distinct parts. For a natural number $k$, let $m_k(d,n)$ denote its $k$th pre-moment, and let $N_d(n)$ denote the generalized Fibonacci sequence used in the source.

**Generalized-Fibonacci pre-moment conjecture.** For each $d$, the $k$th pre-moment $m_k(d,n)$ of $X_{d,n}$ is of the form

$$
a(n)N_d(n)+b(n)N_d(n+1),
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are polynomials in $n$.

This conjecture extends the corresponding fixed-parameter formulas known in the source's earlier work. The source says that experimental evidence verifies the claim, but supplies no proof or database resolution.
parsed.source_name: Anthony Zaleski, “Explicit expressions for the moments of the size of an (n, dn-1)-core partition with distinct parts”, arXiv:1702.05634 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.05634

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

parsed.title: Support conjecture for key polynomials
parsed.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a composition, let $t_{ij}$ swap positions $i$ and $j$, and let $m_{ij}(\alpha)=\alpha+e_i-e_j$. Define $\beta<_\kappa\alpha$ when $\beta$ can be generated from $\alpha$ by a sequence of moves $t_{ij}$ with $\alpha_i<\alpha_j$ and moves $m_{ij}$ with $\alpha_j-\alpha_i>1$. Let $\kappa_\alpha$ be the key polynomial. **Key support conjecture.**

$$
\kappa_\alpha=x^\alpha+\sum_{\beta<_\kappa\alpha}{\sf Key}_{\alpha,\beta}x^\beta,
$$

with ${\sf Key}_{\alpha,\beta}>0$ for every $\beta<_\kappa\alpha$. The source gives no proof or resolution of this stronger support description.
parsed.source_name: Cara Monical, Neriman Tokcan and Alexander Yong, “Newton Polytopes in Algebraic Combinatorics”, arXiv:1703.02583 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.02583

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2017). “Indeed, \[q_{(1)}=s_{(1)}, q_{(2)}=-s_{(1,1)}, q_{(3)}=-s_{(2,1)}.\] Reutenauer's conjecture was later established by W. M. Doran IV .”

parsed.title: The OTE characterization of sticky matroids
parsed.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid. A **modular cut** is a set of flats closed upward and closed under intersections of modular pairs; $M$ is **OTE** (only trivially extendable) if every modular cut other than the empty cut is principal. **OTE characterization conjecture.** A matroid is sticky if and only if it is an OTE matroid. In the finite case, the paper proves equivalence with the Sticky Matroid Conjecture and Kantor's conjecture; the proposed extension to arbitrary rank is described as slightly weaker than the finite Sticky Matroid Conjecture and is not resolved.
parsed.source_name: Winfried Hochstättler and Michael Wilhelmi, “Sticky matroids and Kantor's Conjecture”, arXiv:1704.08478 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.08478

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2017).

parsed.title: The finite-subset covering conjecture for direct products of complete graphs
parsed.statement:
For a positive integer $l$, let $G_l$ have vertex set $\mathbb{N}_0^l$ and an edge between two sequences precisely when they differ in every coordinate. Let $X\subset\mathbb{N}_0^l$ be finite.

**Finite-subset covering conjecture.** There exist sets $X_1,\dots,X_l\subseteq X$ whose union is $X$, such that for every $i$, either $X_i$ is contained in a hyperplane of the form $\{x_i=c\}$ or the induced graph $G_l[X_i]$ is connected.

This is presented as another version of the monochromatic component covering conjecture. The supplied text does not give a resolution status for this formulation, so it remains open in the database.
parsed.source_name: Luka Milićević, “Covering complete graphs by monochromatically bounded sets”, arXiv:1705.09370 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.09370

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

parsed.title: The prime-power conjecture for finite projective planes
parsed.statement:
Let a finite projective plane of order $n$ be a symmetric design with parameters $(n^2+n+1,n+1,1)$.

**Prime-power conjecture.** If a finite projective plane of order $n$ exists, then $n$ is a power of some prime $p$.

Projective planes are known to exist for every prime-power order, while no construction is known for other orders. The conjecture is a long-standing open problem in finite geometry; the Bruck–Ryser–Chowla theorem rules out some non-prime-power orders, but does not settle the general case.
parsed.source_name: Mingchun Xu, “The properties of bordered matrix of symmetric block design”, arXiv:1707.02208 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.02208

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

parsed.title: The algebraic and symmetric shifting Betti-number conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be a simplicial complex over a field $K$ of characteristic zero. Let $I_{\Delta^s}$ and $I_{\Delta^e}$ denote the Stanley–Reisner ideals of the symmetric and exterior shifts of $\Delta$, respectively, and let $\beta_{i,j}$ denote graded Betti numbers.

**Algebraic and symmetric shifting conjecture.** For all $i,j$, 

$$
\beta_{i,j}(I_{\Delta^s})\leq \beta_{i,j}(I_{\Delta^e}).
$$

This conjecture compares the graded Betti numbers arising from symmetric and exterior algebraic shifting; the supplied source does not indicate whether it has been resolved.
parsed.source_name: Luis Pedro Montejano and Luis Núñez Betancourt, “b-vectors of chordal graphs”, arXiv:1709.00474 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.00474

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2017).

parsed.title: Even fans with handles and two spokes removed conjecture
parsed.statement: Let $F^*_n$ be the fan with a handle whose spokes are all edges connected to the hub except the edge connected to the degree $1$ vertex. For all even $n\geqslant 4$, consider $F^*_n$ with any two of these spokes removed. **Even fans with handles and two spokes removed conjecture.** The nim-value of $F^*_n$ with any two spokes removed is $1$. The conjecture is presented as sufficient for proving the wheel graph nim-value conjecture; the source gives no resolution.
parsed.source_name: Cormac O'Sullivan, “A vertex and edge deletion game on graphs”, arXiv:1709.01354 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01354

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2017).

parsed.title: Enumeration conjecture for maximal chains without plus-full-sets in Tamari lattices
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the Tamari lattice, and let $\mathcal{N}_i(n)$ denote the set of maximal chains in $\mathcal{T}_n$ of length $n+i$ with no plus-full-sets. Write $\#\mathcal{N}_i(n)$ for its cardinality.

**Enumeration conjecture.** For all $i\geq-1$,

$$
\#\mathcal{N}_{i}(2i+3)=\prod_{j=1}^{i+1}\binom{3j-1}{2},
$$

and for all $i\geq0$,

$$
\#\mathcal{N}_{i}(2i+2)=\frac{i}{5}\prod_{j=1}^{i+1}\binom{3j-1}{2}.
$$

These formulas are based on numerical evidence and give explicit enumerations for the boundary cases used to study maximal chains in Tamari lattices. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
parsed.source_name: Luke Nelson, “A recursion on maximal chains in the Tamari lattices”, arXiv:1709.02987 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.02987

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2017).

parsed.title: Leth's conjecture on dense almost progressions
parsed.statement:
Fix $t\in\mathbb{N}$ and $c>0$. A set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ **nearly contains a $(t,d,w)$-progression on $[1,n]$** when it contains the almost-progression configuration defined earlier in the source, with common-difference parameter $d$ and error parameter $w$. **Leth's conjecture.** There is $n_0:=n_0(t,c)$ such that, for all $n\geq n_0$, whenever

$$
\delta(A,n)>\frac{1}{(c\log n)^{2\log\log n}},
$$

then $A$ nearly contains a $(t,d,w)$-progression on $[1,n]$ with

$$
\frac{w}{d}<\frac{d}{n},
$$

where $d$ is a power of $2$.

The conjecture is presented as a strengthening of the almost-progression consequences relevant to the Erdős–Turán problem. The source does not state whether it has been resolved.
parsed.source_name: Mauro Di Nasso, Isaac Goldbring and Martino Lupini, “Nonstandard Methods in Ramsey Theory and Combinatorial Number Theory”, arXiv:1709.04076 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.04076

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2017).

parsed.title: Xia–Fang finiteness conjecture for cubic graphical regular representations
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite nonabelian simple group. A **cubic graphical regular representation** (cubic GRR) of $G$ is a Cayley graph of $G$ of valency three whose automorphism group is the right regular representation of $G$.

**Xia–Fang finiteness conjecture.** There are only finitely many finite nonabelian simple groups that have no cubic GRR.

This is a finiteness refinement of the refuted conjecture that every finite nonabelian simple group has a cubic GRR. The source reports verification for alternating groups, Suzuki groups and projective special linear groups of dimension two, while the general statement remains open.
parsed.source_name: Binzhou Xia, “On cubic graphical regular representations of finite simple groups”, arXiv:1709.09157 (2019).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.09157

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2017).

parsed.title: Equivalent Sperner-family formulation of the s-extremal extension conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\mathcal{S}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be a **Sperner family**, meaning that no member of $\mathcal{S}$ contains another, and let $h:\mathcal{S}\to 2^{[n]}$ satisfy $h(S)\subseteq S$ for every $S\in\mathcal{S}$. For $S\in\mathcal{S}$ and $A\subseteq S$, let $\mathcal{Q}_{S,A}$ denote the associated family used in the paper. **Equivalent form of the s-extremal extension conjecture.** There exists $S_0\in\mathcal{S}$ such that

$$
\mathcal{Q}_{S_0,h(S_0)}\not\subseteq\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S_0\}}\mathcal{Q}_{S,h(S)}.
$$

This is stated as an equivalent formulation of the main extension conjecture and is proved in the paper for Sperner families of size at most four; the general conjecture remains open.
parsed.source_name: Christopher Kusch and Tamás Mészáros, “Shattering-extremal set systems from Sperner families”, arXiv:1710.03165 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.03165

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2017). “For maximum classes essentially the same was conjectured by Kuzmin an Warmuth in and proven by Rubinstein and Rubinstein in .”

parsed.title: Li–Feng pendent-path transfer conjecture for the alpha-index
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $u$ be a vertex of $G$, and let $G_{p,q}(u)$ denote the graph obtained by attaching pendent paths of lengths $p$ and $q$ at $u$. For $\rho_{\alpha}$, the alpha-index of a graph, let $\alpha\in[0,1)$. **Pendent-path transfer conjecture.** If $p\geq q+2\geq3$, then

$$
\rho_{\alpha}\left(G_{p,q}(u)\right)<\rho_{\alpha}\left(G_{p-1,q+1}(u)\right).
$$

The assertion is known for $\alpha=0$ and $\alpha=1/2$, and the paper proves it for all $\alpha\in[0,1)$ when $\rho_{\alpha}(G_{p,q}(u))\geq9/4$. Its validity without that additional spectral-radius condition remains open.
parsed.source_name: Vladimir Nikiforov and Oscar Rojo, “On the α-index of graphs with pendent paths”, arXiv:1710.10484 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10484

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

parsed.title: Equivariant Gal conjecture for crystallographic Coxeter complexes
parsed.statement: Let $W$ be a finite crystallographic Coxeter group, and let $\operatorname{Cox}(W)$ be its Coxeter complex. **Equivariant Gal conjecture.** The pair $(\operatorname{Cox}(W),W)$ exhibits the equivariant Gal phenomenon for every finite crystallographic Coxeter group $W$. This is proposed as an equivariant analogue of the paper's Gal-type gamma-positivity results; the source says it is expected to follow from the classification of finite Coxeter groups, while a proof avoiding classification would be more desirable, and gives no proof or resolution.
parsed.source_name: Christos A. Athanasiadis, “Gamma-positivity in combinatorics and geometry”, arXiv:1711.05983 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.05983

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2017). “The following major open problem in geometric combinatorics was posed by \'S. Gal who disproved a more optimistic conjecture, claiming that $h(\Delta, x)$ is real-rooted for every flag triangulation of a sphere.”

parsed.title: Blessing et al.'s broadcast-density isomorphism conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $G_\infty$ be the infinite grid, and for positive integers $t$ and $r$ let $\delta_{t,r}(G_\infty)$ denote the optimal density of a $(t,r)$ broadcast. **Blessing et al.'s conjecture.** For all $t,r\in\mathbb{Z}^+$, the optimal $(t,r)$ and $(t+1,r+2)$ broadcast densities on $G_\infty$ are equal:

$$
\delta_{t,r}(G_\infty)=\delta_{t+1,r+2}(G_\infty).
$$

The conjecture is refuted in this paper by a family of counterexamples, including the stated failure at $(t,r)=(1,1)$ and $(2,3)$; the revised conjecture retains only the case relating $(t,3)$ to $(t-1,1)$ for $t>2$.
parsed.source_name: Benjamin F. Drews, Pamela E. Harris and Timothy W. Randolph, “Optimal (t,r) Broadcasts On the Infinite Grid”, arXiv:1711.11116 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.11116

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

parsed.title: The CGT-value criterion for Left wins in simultaneous Hackenbush
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a **Hackenbush tree**, and let $o_S(G)$ denote its outcome under simultaneous play. If the Conway game-theoretic value of $G$ is greater than $2/3$, then **the CGT-value conjecture.** $o_S(G)$ is a Left win. The preceding discussion establishes this behavior for alternating red-blue Hackenbush stalks, but the claim is stated for arbitrary Hackenbush trees; its general validity is not resolved here.
parsed.source_name: Melissa Huggan, Richard J. Nowakowski and Paul Ottaway, “Simultaneous Combinatorial Game Theory”, arXiv:1810.02870 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.02870

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2018).

parsed.title: Chromatic-choosability conjecture for signed graphs with few vertices
parsed.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a signed graph, with chromatic number $\chi(\Sigma)$ and list chromatic number $\chi_l(\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma$ is **chromatic-choosable** when $\chi_l(\Sigma)=\chi(\Sigma)$.

**Chromatic-choosability conjecture.** If

$$
|V(\Sigma)|\leq \chi(\Sigma)+1,
$$

then $\Sigma$ is chromatic-choosable.

This proposes that the equality between chromatic and list chromatic numbers holds for every signed graph whose order is at most one greater than its chromatic number. The statement is presented as a variant of the paper's main theorem; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
parsed.source_name: Wei Wang and Jianguo Qian, “A generalization of Noel-Reed-Wu Theorem to signed graphs”, arXiv:1810.09741 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.09741

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2018).

parsed.title: BIBD conjecture for binders of odd-prime equiangular tight frames
parsed.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $(p,\ldots,p)$ be a tuple of length $s+1$. Let $\mathcal G(p,\ldots,p)$ denote the corresponding equiangular tight frame, and let its **binder** $\mathcal B(\mathcal G(p,\ldots,p))$ be the collection of simplices associated with that frame. A $(v,k,\lambda)$-BIBD is a balanced incomplete block design with $v$ points, block size $k$, and parameter $\lambda$.

**Binder BIBD conjecture.** The binder of $\mathcal G(p,\ldots,p)$ is a

$$
\left(p^{2(s+1)},p^{s+1},\frac{p^{s+1}-1}{p-1}\right)\text{-BIBD}.
$$

This conjecture generalizes the preceding results for the binder constructions, which establish the claimed design structure in lower-dimensional cases. The general assertion for every odd prime $p$ and every tuple length $s+1$ remains open.
parsed.source_name: Bernhard Bodmann and Emily J. King, “Optimal arrangements of classical and quantum states with limited purity”, arXiv:1811.11513 (2020).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.11513

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2018). “In the complex case, the existence of such extremal cases is an open question posed by Zauner.”

parsed.title: Finite termination of splitting processes for accessible quasi-transitive graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be an accessible connected quasi-transitive locally finite graph. A **splitting process** is any process of repeatedly splitting $G$ as described in the paper.

**Finite termination conjecture.** Every process of splittings must end after finitely many steps.

The conjecture asks whether the terminal factorisation is independent of the particular choices made during splitting. The paper does not establish this for arbitrary splittings; its preceding construction uses a specific invariant tree-decomposition.
parsed.source_name: Matthias Hamann, Florian Lehner, Babak Miraftab and Tim Rühmann, “A Stallings' type theorem for quasi-transitive graphs”, arXiv:1812.06312 (2019).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.06312

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2018).
